title: What Louis Vuitton Taught Me About Belonging
description: A personal and academic analysis of luxury consumption psychology — why the product is almost beside the point, what the space is really selling, and why three people in the same room can feel completely different things.

title: Dressed As Someone Else
description: Can clothing construct a temporary identity that redirects real consumer behavior? A first-person experiment in Toronto testing enclothed cognition, identity extension, and front-stage performance.

title: A Room That Knows You
description: Luxury doesn't begin with the room. It begins the moment you cross the threshold — fifteen seconds before your mind catches up. A study in sensory sequencing, atmospheric design, and how the right environment constructs a version of you that already belongs.

title: The Customer Is Always Right
description: Not all luxury consumers are the same — and the brands that treat them like they are lose all of them. A study in HNW segmentation, why the standard luxury audience model fails, and what it actually takes to serve the top tier correctly.

title: The Price Is The Product
description: How price itself functions as the primary signal — not of value, but of belonging, exclusion, and identity. Why some luxury consumers need the number to be impossible, and what that reveals about the psychology of aspirational consumption at its most concentrated.

title: Time: An Exclusivity
description: Elapsed time is the one luxury input that cannot be manufactured, counterfeited, or bought. Vintage wine, archival fashion, and heritage watches build a framework of temporal scarcity — and a new consumer motive: custodianship.

title: The Luxury of Risk
description: Red Bull isolates the one lever of luxury with nothing to do with the object — the performance of freedom from necessity — and runs it at three dollars a can. An extension of Veblen into conspicuous risk.

title: Motive × Context
description: The same luxury consumer behaves completely differently in different moments — not because they're inconsistent, but because context determines which version of self is active. A three-layer framework for understanding why standard audience archetypes always underperform in luxury brand strategy.

title: The Gradus Framework
description: A diagnostic and integration tool for structural brand inaccessibility. Maps luxury brand defensibility across seven independent filter axes — each taxing a different resource — and stress-tests how resistant each is to being collapsed by a single pressure. Includes entropy analysis, counter-stack defense, and cultivation protocol.

title: The Gradus Diagnostic
description: Run any luxury brand through the Gradus Framework in real time. Scores across all seven axes, labels each filter as structural, performative, or absent, and returns a shareable readout.

title: The Luxury Buyer Profile
description: A six-question diagnostic that places you among the luxury buyer archetypes — Inheritor, Self-Made, Aspirant, Connoisseur, Custodian — with a scored, shareable readout. Runs entirely in your browser.

title: New York as a Living Capital Ecosystem
description: On inequality as mechanism, network logic, and the limits of democratic governance over mobile capital. Why the city's global power and its extreme inequality are not separate phenomena but expressions of the same operating logic — and why the historical record contains exactly three previous addresses and no examples of permanent residence.

title: The Witches They Didn't Burn
description: Salem wasn't about witchcraft. It was about women who had autonomous knowledge, operated outside male-controlled systems, and refused to disappear quietly. A fictional memoir from inside 1692 — and what it reveals about how power has always punished people who don't belong.

title: The Worlds We Secretly Carry
description: Three stories set in the private libraries, grand hotels, and quiet drawing rooms where old money lives. A hand-typeset edition — because some things are better read slowly, on paper.

title: About — Harnoor Jhinzer
description: Who writes the archive — University of Waterloo, Psychology & Business (expected 2028), fieldwork, training at Inside LVMH, Bocconi, LBS, and Duke, and the research agenda: luxury, wealth structures, legal architecture.

title: Gilded Romanticism
description: An original aesthetic framework built on a single refusal — the refusal to choose between ambition and softness, the empire and the rose garden. Six pillars defining a sensibility that holds the corporate and the romantic in the same frame.
